originality_review: Original fourth-wall device built on the Watcher moth (brand easter egg). No known Short uses a floater overlay as the reveal. No real-world claim is made, and the video is labelled as fiction.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Ivy sees a moth-shaped floater wherever she looks. Her eye checks out clear. The floater was never in her eye. It is on the viewer's screen, and it was there the whole time.

hooks.line: There's a moth-shaped floater in my eye. Watch.
hooks.first_visual: Extreme close-up of an eye; a tiny dark moth shape drifts across the frame.

hooks.line: See the speck? It's been there all week.
hooks.first_visual: A bus window view; a small dark speck drifting across the image.

hooks.line: My eye test was clear. The speck wasn't.
hooks.first_visual: A penlight reflected in a pupil.

hooks.line: If it's not in my eye, where is it?
hooks.first_visual: A woman looking straight into the lens.

hooks.line: Don't wipe your screen. It doesn't help.
hooks.first_visual: A small moth silhouette stuck to the image.

setting: Quick tour of the kit: night bus, laundromat, pharmacy back room.
conflict: Ivy wants to be rid of the speck in her vision.
escalation: The speck follows her across locations and she cannot rub it away.
reveal: The penlight shows her pupil is clean; the speck stays fixed to the frame.
emotional_objective: Playful unease; a share-bait 'check your screen' moment.
visual_requirements: speck overlay layer (post, fixed to the frame)
